children: The telecom company's $3.2 bln deal drew strong demand despite global jitters, underscoring the Ambani clan's allure. Investors get their digital ambitions at a dumb pipe valuation multiple. It cushions risks from Jio’s 2020 backers, who paid for the dream and still need an exit.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Ujjaini Dutta on LinkedIn and X.

Jio Platforms, the telecom ⁠unit of India's Reliance Industries, on October 24 set the offer price for its IPO at 1119 rupees per share, at the top end of the marketed range. It values the company's issuance at $3.18 billion and its equity at $109 billion.

Jio drew bids for 4.4 billion shares, about 22 times the 197 million shares ​on offer after three days of bidding, exchange data showed. Qualified institutional buyers bid for nearly 71 ⁠times the shares reserved for them, while foreign institutional investors accounted for 28% of the total bids received. Non-institutional investors subscribed 14 times their share, while retail investors bid for about 3 times their allotted portion.
